alternative_allocation_estimate.baseline_comparison: Current policy reserves 10% evaluation focus and otherwise draws from one 162-item approved-original tier. The pilot keeps the 10% focus but uses 35 percentage points of the remaining allocation for measured debt repair and evidence completion before adding more undifferentiated source volume.
alternative_allocation_estimate.estimate_label: Heuristic proposal from a three-record source-bound sample; not a measured optimum.
alternative_allocation_estimate.scope: authoring assignments only; no change to approval, training admission, or catalog mix_weight

assessment.measured: The current normal authoring pool is concentrated in one 162-task tier, while the deterministic three-task sample spans an approved-normal source with unresolved contract debt, an unapproved source with quantified control failures, and an accepted repair with strong but bounded coverage evidence. All three have catalog mix_weight 1.0, so that field alone does not rank authoring quality or repair cost.

quality_dimensions.cost: Expected review/Racket/dedup cost varies sharply; exact corpus-wide minutes are not measured in this bounded audit.
quality_dimensions.parameter_and_four_query_supervision: None of the three sampled task directories contains a parametric evidence manifest.
quality_dimensions.representation: The sample exposes canonical-profile undercoverage, unreliable declared controls, and bounded morphology support.
quality_dimensions.teachability: Retained evidence ranges from no executable semantic contract to registered-rival rejection; approval alone is not uniform teaching evidence.

bounded_test.design: 40 assignments: 20 current-policy and 20 stratified-pilot, with equal reviewer-minute and protected-Racket-call caps.
metrics: four-query episodes with four distinct visible inputs and Racket-verified labels
unresolved rival or lesson ambiguity rate
reviewer minutes per accepted evidence package
protected Racket calls per accepted evidence package
bounded_test.minimum_before_early_stop: 12 completed or terminal assignments per arm
stopping_rule: Immediately stop any arm for hidden query-answer leakage or an admission-boundary violation.
After at least 12 per arm, stop the pilot as inferior when completion is more than 15 percentage points lower and it has no 20% gain in accepted settings/four-query episodes per 100 Racket calls.
Also stop the pilot when cost per accepted evidence package exceeds 1.5 times current policy without a compensating quality gain.
Prefer the pilot only with at least a 15-point completion/quality gain or a 20% quality-per-cost gain and no safety/admission regression; otherwise finish all 20 per arm and retain the incumbent.

current_policy.distinction: review_full_draw.py chooses authoring work from normal_ids with a separate 1-in-10 evaluation-focus roll; catalog mix_weight is dataset sampling metadata and does not drive that authoring draw.
current_policy.ticket_weight_note: initial heuristics, not measured optimal allocation

limitations: Only three of 300 packet tasks were inspected; one is in the normal authoring pool.
No sampled catalog source explicitly names ARC-GEN or RE-ARC, so this ticket makes no source-specific claim about them.
Retained audit evidence is source-bound and heterogeneous; it is not a fresh corpus-wide rerun.
No model job, corpus-wide Racket battery, draw-policy change, approval, or training admission was performed.
The proposed shares and thresholds are testable estimates, not an optimal-allocation proof.

sample_observations.allocation_read: Approval and catalog weight do not erase current source-bound teaching/evidence debt; a parametric assignment here should budget for contract repair and canonical-profile support.
